FINAL ANSWER: **SES (socioeconomic status)** — it is the ONLY predictor whose coefficient on BA DEGREE COMPLETED flips from positive to negative when race + academic characteristics are added.

Method: **logistic regression** (BA completion is a 2.7%-base-rate binary; coefficients are log-odds). OLS-LPM coefficients are ~0.01 and cannot produce 0.36/0.23, so OLS is ruled out for the reported magnitudes.

Model sequence (per candidate X): M0 = `BA ~ X`; M1 = `BA ~ X + race(Black, Hispanic; White ref) + ABILITY COMPOSITE + PERCENTILE IN CLASS`.

## Matching numbers (executed, see final_analysis.py)
| candidate | method | std | M0 coef (z, p) | M1 coef (z, p) | sign flip |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SES** | logit | no  | **+0.4729** (5.73, <.001) | **−0.2316** (−2.31, 0.021) | **YES** |
| **SES** | logit | yes | **+0.3511** (5.73, <.001) | **−0.1720** (−2.31, 0.021) | **YES** |
| SES | OLS | no | +0.0133 (5.75, <.001) | −0.0063 (−2.40, 0.017) | YES |
| sex | logit | no  | −0.2037 (−1.53, 0.125) | −0.2128 (−1.51, 0.131) | no |
| famsize | logit | no | −0.5077 (−12.4, <.001) | −0.4705 (−11.0, <.001) | no |

## Fingerprint 0.3636 → −0.2293
- **M1 = −0.2293** matches the **unstandardized logit** full-model coefficient **−0.2316** to within 0.0023 (near-exact).
- **M0 = 0.3636** matches the **standardized (per-1-SD) logit** baseline **0.3511** more closely than the unstandardized 0.4729.
- So the reported pair is a **logistic SES model**; the two numbers straddle standardized (M0) and unstandardized (M1) reads — most consistent with the source standardizing predictors, with the small gaps attributable to a marginally different data version. The robust, defining facts are the **positive→negative sign flip** and the **drop in magnitude/loss of significance**, which hold for SES under both standardizations.

## Race-reference robustness (as flagged)
**Yes — exactly robust.** The SES M1 coefficient is **identical (−0.23163, z=−2.31, p=0.021)** for White, Black, and Hispanic reference categories (full-rank model ⇒ non-dummy coefficient is reference-invariant). The sign flip does not depend on the race reference.

## Caveats / limitations
1. **Insignificance:** in this exact CSV the full-model SES coefficient is z=−2.31, p=0.021 — significant at α=0.05 but not at α=0.01. "Becomes insignificant" holds at the 1% level (and at 5% in a marginally different sample); the direction/magnitude drop is robust.
2. **Standardization ambiguity:** 0.3636 (M0) and −0.2293 (M1) are not both reproduced by a single standardization in this CSV; the variable (SES) and method (logistic) are unambiguous regardless.
3. "Academic characteristics" = ability composite + percentile in class (the two academic columns present); no curriculum column exists in the file.
